issues.applicant_position: Testimony generally credible despite vagueness; little education and time passed.
issues.respondent_position: Minister made credibility submissions, which the panel addressed.
issues.result_quote: the panel decided to grant the benefit of the doubt as to the truth of the facts in evidence.

issues.issue: Nexus to s.96: membership in the particular social group of the adoptive family
issues.applicant_position: Family adopted him at 15; he is a member of their particular social group.
issues.result_quote: Consequently, membership in the particular social group of the XXXX family does not establish a nexus under section 96 of the Act.

issues.applicant_position: Threatened, held at gunpoint and kidnapped; fears drug traffickers.
issues.result_quote: the evidence shows that he would be personally subjected to a risk to his life because of an existing conflict between high-level drug traffickers and their accomplices.

issues.applicant_position: Police are linked to traffickers; state protection is not safe.
issues.result_quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant cannot seek state protection without facing a great risk to his life.

issues.issue: Internal flight alternative: whether he faces risk throughout Mexico
issues.applicant_position: Trafficking network operates in all regions, so no safe relocation.
issues.result_quote: The panel concludes that the claimant faces a risk throughout the country.

issues.issue: Exclusion under Art. 1F(b): trafficking as such
issues.applicant_position: Never possessed or controlled drugs; trafficking exclusion does not apply.
issues.respondent_position: Minister referred to trafficking exclusion in submissions.
issues.result_quote: the panel cannot conclude that there are serious reasons for considering that the claimant committed outside Canada the offence of trafficking in a substance as such.

issues.issue: Exclusion under Art. 1F(b): conspiracy to traffic (Jayasekara and Ezokola)
issues.applicant_position: Exclusion must be read narrowly; he was an unknowing collaborator and not a trafficker.
issues.respondent_position: Minister argued exclusion for conspiracy to traffic under Art. 1F(b).
issues.result_quote: the panel concludes that there are serious reasons for considering that the claimant committed outside Canada the offence of conspiracy to traffic
